ex.k: Complete with the correct form of have to.

ex.k: must is often your own opinion. have to is often a rule or a fact. For the past, use had to.

items.s: I ___ call Mum. I haven't spoken to her for weeks.

ex.k: Is the underlined part OK? If not, type the correct form.
mustn't = it's wrong, don't do it. needn't / don't need to = it's not necessary.

items.s: We took a taxi, but the station was close. We ___ (take) a taxi.

ex.k: After insist, suggest, recommend, important that, you can use should + verb or just the base verb.

items.s: The doctor recommended that she ___ (rest) for a week.

ex.k: After suggest, don't use to + verb. Use -ing, or that + subject + verb.

items.s: She suggested ___ to the cinema.
I suggest ___ a taxi.
What do you suggest ___ ?
He suggested ___ for help.
They suggested that I ___ early.
Can I suggest ___ a break?

ex.k: Use should after it's strange/surprising that …, and in if … should for unlikely things.

items.s: It's strange that she ___ (forget). She never forgets anything.
If anyone ___ (call), tell them I'm out.
I was surprised that he ___ (say) that.
If you ___ (need) anything, just ask.

ex.k: After it's time + subject, use the past simple. After it's time, you can also use to + verb.

items.s: It's late. It's time we ___ (go) home.
It's 7.30. It's time ___ (get) up!
Your hair is so long. It's time you ___ (have) a haircut.
It's time the government ___ (do) something about it.
The kids are tired. It's time they ___ (be) in bed.
It's time ___ (start) the meeting.

ex.k: had better is for a specific situation now (or something bad will happen). should is for general advice too.

items.s: We ___ hurry. The shop closes in five minutes.
People ___ eat more vegetables.
You ___ not forget your passport!
It's a great book. You ___ read it some time.
I ___ phone Dad. He's waiting for my call.
It's time we ___ a new car.

ex.k: Use would to talk about imaginary situations.

items.s: I'd love a dog, but I ___ (not / have) time to walk it.
